target_customer: City governments and transit agencies that plan routes, streets and mobility
problem: Transit planners used slow desktop GIS and spreadsheets to design routes; Remix offered a collaborative browser mapping tool that models cost and coverage instantly.
business_model: B2B SaaS annual subscriptions to public agencies

founders.name: Tiffany Chu
prior_employers: San Francisco Department of the Environment (Commissioner)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; Transitmix began as a Code for America project.

founders.name: Sam Hashemi
founders.background_notes: Designer per YC bio; first CEO per press.

founders.name: Danny Whalen
founders.background_notes: Named with the other three as Sequoia seed partners.

technical_complexity.rationale: Browser mapping with fast transit coverage and cost modeling, plus GTFS data handling; standard web mapping with some hard modeling.

defensibility.rationale: Agency workflows and saved plans create stickiness, and government sales cycles slow entrants, but Esri could do much of it.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Esri was noted to do analyses Remix could not but did not copy the product; Remix was bought by Via for a reported 100M dollars in March 2021.

market_need_then: Agencies relied on expensive desktop GIS and spreadsheets; Transitmix drew attention from planners after its 2014 launch and Remix reported over 200 cities in 10 countries by the 2017 Series A.

branding.name_origin: Product began as Transitmix, named in homage to Streetmix, another Code for America hackathon project; Remix is the later short form. Reason for the rename is not stated in sources.
branding.domain_note: Moved from transitmix.net to remix.com; acquisition details not found. remix.com now redirects to Via.
branding.brand_signature: Transitmix, the playful sketch a route tool that grew into an agency product

rebrands.why: Company went from a civic hack to a software company; exact reason not stated

branding.community_and_virality: Transitmix drew coverage from Streetsblog, Human Transit and Planetizen in 2014 and 2015.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong press among planners and a founder brand around Tiffany Chu, with Via keeping the Remix brand after the deal.

pivots.from: Transitmix, a public tool for riders to suggest routes
pivots.why: Route Fifty reports agencies realized the tool made their jobs easier, so it became a software company.

outcome_analysis: Remix turned a Code for America route sketching hack into agency SaaS, won Sequoia as seed and Series A lead, raised about 27 million dollars in total, and was acquired by Via in March 2021 for a reported 100 million dollars with its 65 employees. Success came from a clear pivot to paying agencies, slow incumbent tooling and a founder with civic design credibility.
notes: Seed amount not stated by a primary source; an aggregator lists 2M in 2014-12, unverified, so amount is null. Total raised reported as 27M by TechCrunch (CB Insights 25.65M). Competitor search found only Esri as a later comparison (Governing, undated), so the competitor list is empty. Series A date is May 2017 per aggregator; announcement said 2017-05. Wikipedia and Via press confirm acquisition March 2021.
